Question: What emerging technologies are news publishers using?
Answer: Considering how the volume of online news articles has exploded recently, it is but logical that technology is being leveraged. If you are an avid consumer of news, you would have felt the nagging sensation that a lot of articles now published seem eerily similar in terms of the flow and the tone. That is because it likely has not been written by a human. Artificial Intelligence (AI), Robotics, Machine Learning, NLP, etc are all being used in journalism. Most publishers use some degree of automation to pre-populate drafts based on NLP or Fuzzy Logic and then have the human writers and editors work on refining them for final publication.[1] …Bloomberg news is one of the first adaptors of this automated content. Their program, Cyborg, churned out thousands of articles last year that took financial reports and turned them into news stories like a business reporter. Forbes also uses an AI took called Bertie to assist in providing reporters with first drafts and templates for news stories. The Washington Post also has a robot reporting program called Heliograf. In its first year, it produced approximately 850 articles… Like how The LA Times is using AI to report on earthquakes based on data from the U.S. geological survey and also tracks homicide information on every homicide committed in the city of Los Angeles. The site created by the machine called “Homicide Report” utilizes a robot-reporter with the ability to include in its reports tons of data that includes: the victim’s gender and race, cause of death, officer involvement, neighborhood and year of death. This approach works well for objective reporting in cases that mostly consist of numbers, figures, statistics, and different slices and dices of data — earnings report, economic data, demographic studies, live sports updates, elections.[2] Examples of machine-generated articles from The Associated Press: TYSONS CORNER, Va. (AP) — MicroStrategy Inc. (MSTR) on Tuesday reported fourth-quarter net income of $3.3 million, after reporting a loss in the same period a year earlier. MANCHESTER, N.H. (AP) — Jonathan Davis hit for the cycle, as the New Hampshire Fisher Cats topped the Portland Sea Dogs 10-3 on Tuesday. Bots and automatons have become so significant to reporting that there are separate award categories to recognize their contributions. The Post has an in-house robot reporter called Heliograf, which demonstrated its usefulness with its coverage of the 2016 Summer Olympic Games and the 2016 elections. Last year, thanks to Heliograf, The Post won in the category of Excellence in Use of Bots at the annual Global Biggies Awards, which recognize accomplishments in the use of big data and artificial intelligence. Technology use is not limited to simply preparing first drafts, but also to schedule and publish, take care of SEO and social media publishing, data crunching and analysis, visualizing the larger picture around the article, and to identify fake news. Examples: #1: Washington Post — Knowledge Map (Providing background information) Knowledge Map gives readers an easier way to catch up on ongoing stories by quickly and seamlessly providing relevant background, additional information or answers to frequently asked questions, when the reader wants it. #2: NYT — Editor (Automated tagging and annotation) Editor is an experimental text editing interface that explores how collaboration between machine learning systems and journalists could afford fine-grained annotation and tagging of news articles. Our approach applies machine learning techniques interactively, as part of the writing process, rather than retroactively. This approach can offload the burden of work to the computational processes, and can create affordances for journalists to augment, edit and correct those processes with their knowledge. #3: BBC — Juicer (Automated RSS feed monitoring and aggregation) BBC Juicer is a news aggregation 'pipeline'. It ingests news articles and extracts the best from them - well, just like a fruit juicer does. BBC Juicer pipeline is watching RSS feeds of news outlets. When a new article is published on one of these RSS feeds, BBC Juicer scrapes the news article, both raw text and metadata (e.g. date, time, title, news source ...). In the next step BBC Juicer identifies and tags concepts mentioned in the article text making them searchable and therefore useful for trend analysis. Question: How do you stop thinking you're a failure?
Answer: Here is a really poignant strip (The Two Wolves) from Zen Pencils that puts into perspective the right way to deal with one’s internal strifes and demons. You are what you think you are. I AM A FAILURE. Remove the last two words. I AM. Which is an absolute. Add anything after these two words. Make it yours. I AM happy. I AM doing the best I can. I AM going to do better. I AM a good person. That is it. Do not hold yourself to impossible standards. Success is a personal definition. Someone who is extremely successful in your opinion might feel like a complete loser themselves. Due to globalization, we now compare ourselves with everyone else. Without considering that a lot of it is due to our personal circumstances, which are outside of our control. More people are afflicted with Impostor syndrome than you think. Findings of the study, co-authored by Brigham Young University professors Jeff Bednar, Bryan Stewart, and James Oldroyd, revealed that 20 percent of the college students in their sample suffered from very strong feelings of impostorism. Surprisingly, the study also reveals that perceptions of impostorism lack a significant relationship with performance. This means that individuals who suffer with the impostor syndrome are still capable of doing their jobs well, they just don't believe in themselves. Researchers also explain that social-related factors impact impostorism more than an individual's actual ability or competence. "The root of impostorism is thinking that people don't see you as you really are," said Stewart, an accounting professor at BYU and co-author on the study. "We think people like us for something that isn't real and that they won't like us if they find out who we really are." On any objective scale, all of these students are in the top decile of success, but since they incessantly compare themselves with their other exceptional peers, they feel otherwise. Despite being able to do their jobs well, their lack of self-esteem and this crippling feeling of “not being good enough” affects their evaluation of their self-worth. A lot of extremely successful folks persevere in the face of initial failures and setbacks — Here's what the world's most successful people think about failure, including the likes of Walt Disney who was initially dismissed for “lacking imagination and having no good ideas” and JK Rowling whose first script for the Harry Potter franchise was rejected by over a dozen publishers. So, the simplest way to stop thinking of yourself as a failure is to remember than you are not. You might have failed, yes. But failure isn’t permanent. You can either treat your previous snafus as learning lessons and use them to eventually become successful. Or you can concede defeat and become a quitter. Either way, you won’t be a failure, just someone who stopped before they succeeded.

Question: How does going to an IIM serve your purpose of becoming an entrepreneur?
Answer: It doesn’t. What the IIMs offer are: In all of this, there is no elaborate entrepreneurship strategy. Most IIMs do have their own in-house start-up incubators wherein they provide financial and mentoring support to aspiring entrepreneurs. For example, IIMA has a program called IIMAvericks. The IIMAvericks Entrepreneur - in - Residence (EIR) Program supports early stage entrepreneurs from top institutes in India who are looking to start up. The program will provide mentoring & financial support to founders to take the road less travelled and start-up. The grant will help the entrepreneur sustain herself during this crucial period, and help them focus more on the business. The program is currently offered to entrepreneurs from IIMA, IITM, IITB, BITS Pilani and other institutes who have started/ are starting up anywhere in India. CIIE.CO | The Innovation Continuum follows a virtual incubation model & it is not necessary for the start-up to be stationed in Ahmedabad. What's on offer? 1. CIIE.CO | The Innovation Continuum shall pay the entrepreneur a monthly stipend of INR 30,000 for a period of a year. 2. CIIE.CO | The Innovation Continuum shall assist in raising seed funding for the start-up as and when the need arises. 3. CIIE.CO | The Innovation Continuum shall help appoint an industry expert as an advisor to the start-up as and when required. 4. The selected start-up shall have access to all CIIE.CO | The Innovation Continuum resources, including but not limited to incubation space in Ahmedabad, complimentary/preferential access to major tech ecosystems like Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud services etc. and a network of experts. I know a few folks who picked this option over the normal placements route. The moratorium period for the student loan is also extended for the folks choosing the start-up route. If you want to really pursue entrepreneurship, the IIMs might not be the best route to take. Your entire first year will be crammed with academic and extra-curricular asks. You will rarely have the time or the energy to ideate or test a new business idea. You can do that in the second year though, but it would be ideal to have a plan in mind before you enter college to make the most of it. It will, however, allow you access to a large pool of people to choose your founding team from. The courses will give you a good understanding of all that goes into running a business (but will be far more effective if you already have substantial work experience). And the IIMAvericks program is just a cherry on top that allows you a one-year period to bounce your ideas off of the right set of people, a decent stipend for personal expenses, inroads into your seed funding, and overall industry connects to nurture and grow your idea. But ultimately, it will all depend on your clarity of thought and willingness to hustle without any certainty of rewards for your efforts. Basically, the same hurdles any entrepreneur faces.

Question: Has India's 'Starving Yogi' and the extraordinary claim that he has not had anything to eat or drink for nearly 70 years been disproved?
Answer: The onus of the proof here lies with the claimant. All these claims of mystics living for hundreds of years in the Himalayas, or not having eaten in decades is all a charade designed to dupe the unassuming ones. It doesn’t mean that what the late Prahlad Jani had achieved was a small feat. He indeed had so much control over his body that he needed the bare minimum to survive. But the entire claim of not having eaten or drunk anything for seventy years is totally bogus — The man who says he hasn't eaten or drunk for 70 years: Why are eminent doctors taking him seriously? Mr. Jani has only been under strict observation twice. Both times under the supervision of the same doctor. Both times for only 15 days. Even during those 15 days, he was allowed to bathe (yes, with water) and sunbathe (which he claims provides him with sustenance). The people who observed him never published their findings in any scientific journal. Nor did they allow any third party to investigate the setting in which he was kept. All we have to go on are their words. They promised to make the findings from the study public, but that never came to pass — DIPAS concludes observational study on ‘Mataji' However, during the second stint of him being monitored, he lost about 4 kgs of weight — https://www.iosrjournals.org/iosr-jrme/papers/Vol-7%20Issue-5/Version-1/J0705015587.pdf For example, the yogi lost some weight during the study and this would be evidence that his claims are wrong, said the head of the Austrian Skeptics Society Dr. Ulrich Berger. Mathematican and head skeptic Berger did more research than James Randi on the case and actually read through the published study and the presentation of Dr. Shah and found that "the daily weight varied between 42 und 38 kilos". So Dr. Berger published as counterevidence that Jani lost 4 kilos from day one to the end of the study. If he lost almost 10% of his body weight during the term of the study, he should have completely disappeared in just 5–6 months. He was also not under 24*7 CCTV surveillance as he was allowed to meet devotees and sunbathe without much supervision. Sanal Edamaruku characterized the experiment as a farce for allowing Jani to move out of the CCTV cameras' field of view, claiming that video footage showed Jani was allowed to receive devotees and to leave the sealed test room for sunbathing. Edamaruku also said that the gargling and bathing activities were insufficiently monitored. Edamaruku was denied access to the site where the tests were conducted in both 2003 and 2010, and accuses Jani of having "influential protectors" responsible for denying him permission to inspect the project during its operation, despite having been invited to join the test during a live television broadcast. Considering all of that, it is a great feat of human endurance, but no miracle. After all, Gandhiji fasted for days on end multiple times during the Independence movement, the longest lasting 21 days. If he really was a human miracle as he had claimed, he should have agreed to do a much longer independent study to prove his extraordinary claims.

The flashback battle scene of Darkseid’s first invasion is rumored to be more than 15 minutes long with some epic Zeus and Green Lantern scenes. Finally, we might just get to see the SEVEN in action as there is a strong possibility that Martian Manhunter is introduced in the movie (which you know should have been the case since the promotions have forever teased “UNITE THE SEVEN”). All in all, the Snyder Cut will be the unadulterated, untarnished vision of Synder brought to life. It won’t stick to the studio whims of “no more than 150-minute runtime”, being more than 4 hours long. The reshoots of Whedon would be buried like they should have been. Each character gets their due on the screen. After all, this isn’t Synder’s first rodeo. His Director’s Cut of Watchmen was received far more positively than the theatrical version (Improving On Perfection: Watchmen - Director's Cut (Blu-ray)), despite only incorporating 24 extra minutes of footage. The ZSJL would be twice as long, with just not extra footage but also undoing Whedon’s damage to a large extent.

Question: Should Black Panther be recast?
Answer: Obviously. Financially, Black Panther was a superhit and it goes without saying that the studio is not going to give up on such a hot property due to the demise of the lead actor. But that isn’t the most important angle here. Black Panther wasn’t just Chadwick (Rest In Power). It was the effort of thousands of actors, directors, writers, cinematographers, VFX folks, editors, sound artists, crew, etc. Nullifying all plans for a sequel would be a disservice to all of these others who poured their hearts and souls into the movie. And even Chadwick wouldn’t have had it otherwise. The dude battled with cancer for 4 years, all the while taking up the mantle of the first black superhero. He knew what he was doing. He knew he was taking up a legacy that means a lot to people of color worldwide. Portraying Black Panther was his honor. And his duty. And he discharged that with every ounce of his being. Despite fighting his own body, he made sure to never stop being the inspiration that he had signed up for. He visited children fighting the same fight, just to brighten up their day. It took Marvel dozen-plus movies to finally produce one with a black lead. And an amazing one at that. Imagine being a comic/superhero fan and finding that all the superheroes, the bastions of humanity look different that you. That the only dude who shares your skin tone is a side-kick (for now). That there has not been a single movie that celebrates your culture. And then Black Panther comes out in all its glory, replete with the colors and the clothes and the history of you. That is how black people, and especially kids, reacted to this cultural phenomenon. Chadwick would like to see this legacy continued. To do justice by the King of Wakanda on screen. He should be celebrated. He should be respected. He should be recast.

Question: Can DCEU take over Marvel in the next decade?
Answer: It absolutely can. The biggest mistake the execs over at WB did was to blindly imitate MCU and rush to catch up by planning a haphazardly planned series of movies and interfering too much with the directors’ creative vision. For example, Snyder had a 5-6 movie plan for the first JL storyline — Zack Snyder Confirms Justice League Five-Movie Arc. WB execs were playing catch up to Marvel and wanted to get the Justice League team out there as soon as possible. Snyder didn't want Justice League released as soon as it was as his plan was to follow the story of Superman. Daly says Snyder wanted to do five or six movies that started with Superman being the reluctant hero leading to the Superman everyone is familiar with, i.e. a boy scout version approved by the president. Daly says the arc started with Superman with the idea of him being a reluctant apathetic hero who didn't know if he belonged on earth or wanted to save people, leading to the Superman we all know, but Daly says we never got a chance to see it. Daly also says Snyder's 5-6 movie plan consisted of Man of Steel, Batman vs. Superman, Justice League, Man of Steel 2, and a two-part Justice League (JL 2 and 3). Daly says a lot of things were left out from Snyder's true vision, that Snyder got a raw deal, and that Snyder had a lot going on moving forward. Daly also confirms that Aquaman did save Clark Kent from the oil rig in Man of Steel and a lot was left out from Snyder's original plans for Batman vs. Superman as well. After Snyder’s departure from JL, Whedon was brought in to finish the movie and cut it down to 120–150 mins, leading to a lot of essential scenes especially involving Barry and Victor. Whedon also did a lot of reshoots, totally changing the tone of the movie. The eyesore red sky hue in the final battle (Justice League's Snyder Cut Final Battle Will Differ in Color from Original), the cringy scene where the Flash falls and gropes Diana (Joss Whedon Reportedly Threatened To Destroy Gal Gadot's Career If She Didn't Do This Suggestive Scene For ‘Justice League,’ And Some Twitter Posts Confirm It), the CGI de-mustached Superman scenes (Superman with a mustache from Justice League reshoots leaks), the removal of pivotal scenes featuring Cyborg, the one Snyder said was the heart of the movie, and many more. In the end, due to the studio meddling and Whedon’s absolute mauling of the movie, what we received was a sub-standard version of a tale that could have been amazing. But now, with AT&T coming into the picture and the #ReleaseTheSynderCut movement finally bearing fruit, we will see the true vision of Zach Snyder brought to life. During this time, WB has also finally let go of the idea of a MCU-esque cinematic universe over a broader multiverse where disconnected stories can take place since they transpire in different universes. That is how we had the Joker movie right after Suicide Squad and before Birds of Prey. That is how we will have Batfleck reappear in the Flash (Ben Affleck Will Return as Batman in The Flash) while Battinson debuts in The Batman. And he will not be the only Batman in the movie. Keaton’s Batman would make an appearance too. After BvS and JL fiasco, WB has finally found a good rhythm. Aquaman was a billion-dollar box office success. Wonder Woman was a box office hit and a critic favorite rolled into one. Joker is the most profitable superhero movie of all time, raking in more than a billion on a $60 mn budget, delivering 16x returns (Box Office: ‘Joker’ Becomes First R-Rated Movie to Hit $1 Billion). Shazam, though not a smash hit at the box office was a really different, fresh take on the superhero genre, and was adored by viewers and critics alike. The Suicide Squad by James Gunn looks very promising and colorful, unabashed of the weirdness of its comic book roots. We have a Flash movie in the works, and a Black Adam feature starring Dwayne Johnson (the hottest name in Hollywood right now) as the titular anti-hero. WW84 looks really good. The Batman trailer was simply amazing, promising a close look at the Detective side of the Caped Crusader. At the same time, Marvel’s first cinematic iteration is done. RDJ and Evans are no more a part of it. The original roster has retired. And the next generation of superheroes will need to find their own footing first before being able to reap the same level of adulation and success as their predecessors. With the right setup, a proper plan, and loads of patience, we might eventually get another amazing cinematic experience over the next few years.

Question: Does Wikipedia have a left-wing bias?
Answer: Yes. The strong left-wing bias of Wikipedia is mostly propagated through the Fallacies of Omission. While the contents of the articles are rooted in proper sources and citations, it is often through careful selection of “what to include and what not to” that shapes up the tone of the various articles in line with the inherent biases of its super editors. An HBR piece from 2014 (Wikipedia Is More Biased Than Britannica, but Don’t Blame the Crowd) outlined the start of the decline of neutrality at the open-source encyclopedia. Greenstein and Zhu borrowed this taxonomy of partisan terms and counted their use in pairs of Wikipedia and Britannica articles on the same subject. They calculated bias as the absolute difference between the number of Democratic terms and the number of Republican ones. For example, if an article contained 10 terms associated with Democrats and only three associated with Republicans, its bias score would be seven. They found that Wikipedia is significantly more biased than Britannica by this measure, and a bit more left-leaning. Larry Sanger, co-founder, wrote a detailed piece earlier this year — Wikipedia Is Badly Biased. The Barack Obama article completely fails to mention many well-known scandals: Benghazi, the IRS scandal, the AP phone records scandal, and Fast and Furious, to say nothing of Solyndra or the Hillary Clinton email server scandal—or, of course, the developing “Obamagate” story in which Obama was personally involved in surveilling Donald Trump. Meanwhile, as you can imagine, the idea that the Donald Trump article is neutral is a joke. Just for example, there are 5,224 none-too-flattering words in the “Presidency” section. By contrast, the following “Public Profile” (which the Obama article entirely lacks), “Investigations,” and “Impeachment” sections are unrelentingly negative, and together add up to some 4,545 words—in other words, the controversy sections are almost as long as the sections about his presidency. Or to take an up-to-the-minute issue, the LGBT adoption article includes several talking points in favor of LGBT adoption rights, but omits any arguments against. On all such issues, the point is that true neutrality, to be carefully distinguished from objectivity, requires that the article be written in a way that makes it impossible to determine the editors’ position on the important controversies the article touches on. Apart from political bias, Wikipedia is also biased against women — Why is Wikipedia biased against women? And can it be changed?. But Wikipedia, to put it bluntly, is a man’s world. In a 2011 survey (the latest comprehensive stocktake), the Wikimedia Foundation found that less than 10% of Wikipedia’s contributors identify as women. This lack of inclusive participation has contributed to an alarming content gap: recent research indicates that only around 17% of biographies on Wikipedia are about women. These surveys don’t give numbers of articles about trans women, Māori women and other women of colour, or non-binary people, but we can fairly assume these groups are even more underrepresented. When women do get biographies, they tend to be more focussed on the subject’s domestic life, relationships, and family, than men’s (which, unsurprisingly, tend to focus more on career achievements). The recent debacle over the Delhi riots article also displays its strong ant-Hindu leaning — Has Wikipedia been compromised to the Left loonies? Investigation reveals that the online encyclopedia is in the clutches of Left and anti-Hindu elements It does on about the prolific editor DBigXray and his years-long attempt at distorting current events. Earlier to the Delhi riots page, the same DBigXray has shown his Hindu and India hatred in several instances. For instance, he had removed “Pandit” from Pandit Deen Daya Upadhyay’s page. He had also removed anything positive about Deen Dayal Upadhyay on the page. He added ‘Militant’ to the Article about Veer Savarkar. He had also added the false information that Veer Savarkar had a physical relationship with Nathuram Godse, the assassin of MK Gandhi. The user also added an entire section to the article about ‘Jai Shree Ram’ where he added the edit that says it has turned into a “murder cry”. He had changed “Martyred” to “Killed” in the Wikipedia article about Captain Saurabh Kalia, who was mutilated and murdered by Pakistan. So when you use Wikipedia, be cautious. It is the best place to start learning about a topic, but should not shape your entire stance on anything. Cross-check the references, pay heed to the tone of the article. It is also high time that the online publicly-edited encyclopedia gets proper competition to ensure that it doesn’t abuse its monopolistic powers.

Question: Was the Rhea Chakraborty interview with Rajdeep Sardesai fully scripted?
Answer: “Interview”? That was not an interview, but a meticulously planned PR activity. The entire setting of the show, the way the questions were framed, and the entire flow of the discussion was an attempt to stir up sympathy for Rhea. Now, she is innocent until proven guilty. And that is how she should be treated. The social media pitchfork army has no right to be the judge, jury, and executioner. No one does. But that entire 90 min episode isn’t the objective truth either. Rajdeep’s questions were totally leading. At the very start, he talks about how Rhea would have dreamt of becoming a Bollywood superstar but is now “India’s most wanted”, a “villain” in a twisted series of events, subtly insinuating that successful people cannot be criminals. He attempts the sympathy-bait by focusing on her ambitions, laying down the groundwork for an hour and a half long attempt at appealing to the audience’s emotion. The way most of the responses were framed makes it abundantly clear that they were totally rehearsed. “The day we were leaving for our Europe trip, he told me and his friends and family that he is afraid of flying because he is claustrophobic. This is when he told us he takes a medicine that makes him feel better — modafinil. That medicine was always with him and he took it before the flight took off.” Quite an elaborate story. When that claim was debunked after Ankita Lokhande, Sushant’s ex, shared photos of Sushant in the cockpit of a Boeing, Rhea replied that the claustrophobia was the reason why Sushant wanted to learn how to fly a plane. At one point, Rajdeep asked the most loaded question, literally claiming that Sushant “possibly” suffered from Bipolar Disorder (or at the very least clinical depression or any form of a mental disorder), a bold statement from someone who is not the said person’s fucking doctor. There is no room for discussion in his statement. As if by saying it out loud, he will be able to convince everyone that Sushant’s death was indeed a suicide despite the entire mist surrounding the exact nature of his demise and the suspicious chain of events leading up to the tragedy. Rajdeep has a long history of being on the side that is ultimately proven wrong. Almost three decades to this day, he wrote a glowing tribute to Dawood, employing the same tactics he does here to exonerate Dawood of his role in the Mumbai blasts. The opening para ends thus. “In the lexicon of Hindu militancy, he symbolises the Muslim as a criminal with extraterritorial loyalty.” He tried painting Dawood as a patriot by invoking Cricket at the finish/ Mr. Thackeray has always seen support for the Indian Cricket Team when it is playing Pakistan to be a mark of a true patriot. He might be intrigued to learn that during the one-day internationals in Sharjah, one man who speaks fluent Marathi has been spotted waving the tricolour and vociferously cheering the Indian Team. His name is Dawood Ibrahim." Tries his very best to say, “look guys, his foremost henchmen were all Hindus”. Unfortunately, a section of Hindus has begun to be carried away by the rhetoric. In the process, they are forgetting a cardinal principle of the underworld; it is as Mr. Samra points out, more cosmopolitan than the society. The only religion it knows is money. Dawood’s own case confirms this mercenary-instinct. A majority of his key men like Chota Rajan, Raj Koli, Bhai Thakur, Anna Shetty are Hindus. Dawood’s own rise in the underworld was built on the systematic decimation of the Pathan gang of Karim Lala. Here’s his dedication to Afzal Guru, the 2001 Parliament attack case convict. Did anyone expect better from him this time?

Question: What are your thoughts on the new Batman teaser?
Answer: HOLY BONE-CRUNCHING BEATDOWN, BATMAN! The problem with a character like Batman is that he is just too mainstream. As such, every time there is a new iteration, people are quick to judge and condemn because they have their own unique tunnel vision of what the character should look and talk and move like. And these predispositions are mostly based on the recent incarnations of The Caped Crusader. The expectations from the actor as soon as their name is revealed are so high that the reality often falls short. It’s the most classic case of millions simultaneously judging the book by its cover. But here we are. And the naysayers have been proved wrong once more. What we have in the Batman trailer is a younger, inexperienced Batman who has still not come to terms with the death of his parents. What we are looking at is the rough draft for what will eventually become the world’s greatest hero and his rogue gallery. Matt Reeves confirmed so.[1] “It’s actually in a weird way the origins of a lot of our Rogues Gallery characters. Selina isn’t Catwoman yet, that’s actually part of the journey. Oz is not yet the kingpin that he’s going to become, he’s The Penguin and in fact doesn’t like being called The Penguin. And The Riddler is just emerging for the first time.” Farrell looks simply unrecognizable as Penguin. Catwoman is just a burglar with a woolen kitty-eaned full face mask. And that beatdown at the end, points to a far more Brutal Batman than we are accustomed to on the silver screen. Pattinson’s voice sounds amazing. Unlike Bale’s growl. The overall direction that Reeves is taking is amazing. We are finally getting a deranged, psychopathic Riddler played by the fabulous Paul Dano. Instead of just comedy shticks and giggles, this is a Riddler that will push the Dark Knight to the limits of his cognitive ability. Finally, a Batman who is just not cool gadgets and martial arts moves, but the world’s greatest detective skills. It’s long overdue that the casual fandom is reminded that the Riddler is a force to be reckoned with. That he deduced Batman’s identity but chose to not reveal it because “a riddle that everyone knows the answer to is worthless”. Finally, what a fantastic riddle to start off. I AM THE HYPE! Question: I'm asymptomatic COVID-19 positive (report received today) residing in Gurgaon. Will authority come at my door? I'm anxious and yet to tell my parents about this.

Question: Why are freelancers obliged to pay taxes? They don't have office space, they don't use any natural resources. Why is it important for them to pay tax only because they are in your country?
Answer: Taxation is complex. There is an economic concept of Price discrimination. In an ideal world, sellers would love nothing more than to charge their customers the highest they are willing to pay. That would maximize profits. If there is a great electric toothbrush in the market, I might be willing to pay $20 for it, but others might not be so inclined. So the company has to fix the price somewhere in between, say $8. This way, part of the profits from the ideal scenario is passed on to the consumers in the form of surplus, and part of it is lost as DWL (Dead Weight Loss). Personalized pricing is called first-degree price discrimination. However, to implement it would be extremely impractical and costly. Companies would need to know exactly how much a consumer is willing to pay for a service or product and have some mechanism to deliver the same to them personally. Similarly, taxation ideally should be in a manner that is just to all. When VIPs go out, entire roads are barricaded. They are using more of the common resources than an average citizen who has to wait for the traffic to clear. But there is no way to implement a perfect “first-degree” tax system. So the government simplifies things through a tiered tax structure along with deductions and benefits to make it as equitable as possible. That is why you have higher marginal tax rates for richer people, Ecotax for industries that have a greater negative effect on the environment, etc. As a freelancer, you might be using lesser resources than an employed person. But not NOTHING as you claim. You are still utilizing electricity that has to come from somewhere. Or availing government services and other public resources. If you head out for some work-related reason, you are using the roads and public transport. Yes, your workspace is the same as your living accommodation, but again companies do pay property and maintenance taxes for their corporate offices. So your assumption is not entirely valid. And the alternate where everyone is taxed in accordance with their utilization of public resources is a practically impossible problem. In the meantime, you can always optimize your business through tax deductions, allowed deferrals, depreciation, and a tax-optimal salary structure for yourself.

Name: Deepak Mehta
Question: What is something that people assume about you but isn't actually true?
Answer: Based on how active I am on Quora and how vocal I am on a whole range of issues, people who don’t know me assume I am an extroverted person who loves to talk and debate. But the truth couldn’t be further that assertion. The only reason I write on Quora is that writing as a medium is something that really resonates with my personality. It allows me the peace of mind to gather my thoughts and the time to articulate them the precise way I want. I am petrified of public speaking. Even at social events, I usually prefer to keep quiet and listen rather than talk. I am highly introverted and my favorite day is one where I am all alone, without any human company. A lot of thoughts go through my mind at any given instance in time requiring a conscious effort to stop and focus before I lose my train of thought. There are very few people in whose company I feel comfortable enough to be who I am. And it takes quite some time for me to develop that level of comfort with someone new. Some also assume I am really organized, which is true to some extent. But then there are pockets of my life that are in total disarray. There are personal projects I started years ago which are still incomplete because I just cannot picture the road to completion. There are answers in my drafts that lingered on for years and I just can’t seem to even delete them and move on. A lot of super-organized folks have that one closet at their place which is just stuffed with everything that doesn’t fit into their blueprint, and I am no different. People also presume that I am a stoic who bases everything on facts and data and inferences and the scientific method. But nah. I cry when I watch a really emotional movie. Question: Do metro cities in India like Mumbai and Bengaluru need to lay restrictions on people migrating from other states/villages like Hong Kong?
Answer: No, please. The entire idea of having a country is that all of its citizens have the right to free movement. States and districts and counties are good to have from a governance perspective, but the entirety of the nation should allow people to freely move within its boundaries to pursue their goals and ambitions. The question we should be asking is why does India still have only a handful of big cities with ample opportunities for people? For any highly skilled job, the options that an Indian has can be counted on one’s fingers — Delhi, Mumbai, Pune, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru. And Ahmedabad, Vishakhapatnam, Chandigarh, Mysore, Cochin to some extent. And they are already stretched to their limits in terms of population and resource constraints. Considering that India is home to more than one-sixth of the world population, we need more such centers of economic development. This will not only ensure more uniform development but will also ease real estate prices in the current metros. India has 46 cities with a population of more than a million. By contrast, the US has only 10. And yet the total GDP of these 10 US cities will probably be equal to that of entire India. If we could just get all of the million+ cities in India to produce $10k of GDP per capita, we would have a 100 million-strong population contributing 1 trillion to the Indian GDP (more than double of the current). At the same time, we have to realize that most states in India have not been able to develop any major anchor cities. UP with a population of 200 million does not a have single center of commerce or service. The same goes for Bihar, Jharkhand, MP, Chhattishgarh, Rajasthan. As such, there is a dire need to create more “centers of excellence” spread throughout the country to have a more inclusive growth trajectory in the future. To achieve the same, the following would be needed: We need to have state-level accountability on long-term infrastructure development. The central government should be held accountable too — Whatever happened to SMART cities?

Question: On days like this, it takes everything in me not to commit suicide. I feel like I have nobody who cares about me. How can I help myself?
Answer: I am sorry about this. I truly am. I have never felt this way, and I cannot even begin to comprehend what you are going through. All I can offer are a few words of comfort. #1: Suicide won’t fix anything Don’t get me wrong. I am not trying to downplay the struggles that people go through, some so monumental that death seems the only escape. No. I will also not try to appeal to your emotional side . “Think of your loved ones, how much they will hurt!”. NO! I want you to think selfishly. What happens when you die? The pain goes away, but so does every other sensation. This is the only life you get. Once you die, you cease to exist. The world will go on without you. Some of them will be affected. But temporarily. Time heals. A year or two later, your friends and family will still remember you. Sporadically. Probably on your birth/death days. But there’s still no you. No afterlife. No second chances. You don’t become a ghost. Or a non-physical consciousness. The universe won’t miss you. Are things that bad? If your family sucks, move away. If your spouse is abusive, leave them and call the cops. If you are clinically depressed, give medical science a chance. The universe existed for billions of years before you came around and will continue for billions more once you are no more. But for you, the only years out of these billions that matter are the partly 80 or so. That is an unfairly minuscule time period. Is anything worth shortening it even more? Trust me, nothing is worth it. #2: It isn’t brave Suicide isn’t bravery. It is the culmination of a lifetime of fighting one’s demons. It is the final cry after all others have been ignored. It is the cumulative failure of the human race. Survivors often regret their decision in midair, if not before. Ken Baldwin and Kevin Hines both say they hurdled over the railing, afraid that if they stood on the chord they might lose their courage. Baldwin was twenty-eight and severely depressed on the August day in 1985 when he told his wife not to expect him home till late. “I wanted to disappear,” he said. “So the Golden Gate was the spot. I’d heard that the water just sweeps you under.” On the bridge, Baldwin counted to ten and stayed frozen. He counted to ten again, then vaulted over. “I still see my hands coming off the railing,” he said. As he crossed the chord in flight, Baldwin recalls, “I instantly realized that everything in my life that I’d thought was unfixable was totally fixable—except for having just jumped.” (Jumpers) There are a lot of emotions people are thought to experience just before death - tranquility, regret, clarity of thought. Maybe in that split second before your body hits the curb, a moment that seemingly stretches for minutes and hours, you can finally clear your head and see everything for what it truly is. Now imagine being in that moment, a clock hand's tick away from death. And suddenly realizing what an absolute idiot you have been. Imagine the panic. The angst. Would you want to go through it? Make a decision that is almost certainly irreversible? Are things really that bad? Or is it just the overly-cynical you? Is the opinion of strangers and people who won’t even think of you ever again so important? And the ones who truly love you? Do they deserve the pain you will leave them with? What if the future is not as bleak as you think and you meet a gorgeous woman and spend half a century together, surrounded by ecstatic love?What if everything just falls in place one fine day and makes all of your struggles worth it Would you forego years of happiness (even in pockets) for an eternity of nothingness? “But in the end, one needs more courage to live than to kill himself.” ― Albert Camus Be courageous, won’t you? #3: You’ve got help For a long time, suicide wasn’t discussed. Some cultures considered it a dishonor and even refused the victim a proper burial. Some exalted it as a brave step, especially when it was committed in the line of duty to the state. And a few even encouraged it as a pious action since it freed the subject from a lifetime of pain and suffering. However, we know better now. The human race, over the last few decades, has become more aware of the reasons behind suicide. We have become more considerate towards the ones who decide to walk down this path because they see no other. We have made efforts to provide support and treatment wherever possible to people who might exhibit suicidal tendencies. If you tag any question with the Suicide topic on Quora, the site automatically adds the below text. If you search for “suicide” on Google, this is the first result that is displayed. Even corporations, non-living entities, are making efforts to do their part in standing alongside people, letting them know that they are not alone. Countless NGOs and self-help groups work around the clock trying to help anyone who might need it. For the last 15 years, the 10th of September has been observed as World Suicide Prevention Day in an effort to spread awareness and send out a message of solidarity. You’re not alone. #4: You can change things One of the saddest things I have learned about recently is the existence of Suicide bags. But you can change that. Don’t keep a “suicide kit”. Build a “life kit”. A box of things that you love. Photographs from the yesteryears that bring a smile to your face. Songs that uplift your mood. Old chats from friends you adore. The phone numbers of people who’ve always been there for you. Pieces of chocolates. Memorabilia from old lovers. Your favorite books. Movie stubs. Art you’ve created. Videos of your birthday when you were young. Video games and movies from past summer afternoons. Your old sports jersey. Anything to remind you that things were not always this bad. And to assure you that they won’t remain this way. Promise me.

Question: Why don’t Indian schools teach astrology as part of the syllabus if it is that important to decide the life of 2 people?
Answer: Because it isn’t (important) and it doesn't (decide someone's life). One of the most well-known Indian astrologers, Bejan Daruwalla, recently died after contracting COVID. I am sure he didn’t predict it. Astrology is a farce. They can only spew out extremely vague statements about the future which can be interpreted in any number of ways, and nothing about the discipline is rooted in science or logic. You would do equally well tossing a coin to make life choices instead of hiring an astrologer for a hefty sum.[1] There’s very little scientific proof that astrology is an accurate predictor of personality traits, future destinies, love lives, or anything else that mass-market astrology claims to know. For example, in a 1985 study published in the journal Nature, Dr. Shawn Carlson of University of California, Berkeley’s Physics department found that seasoned astrologers were unable to match individual’s star chart with the results of a personality test any better than random chance; in a second test, individuals were unable to choose their own star charts, detailing their astrologically divined personality and character traits, any better than chance. A smaller 1990 study conducted by John McGrew and Richard McFall of Indiana University’s Psychology department and designed with a group of astrologers, found that astrologers were no better at matching star charts to the corresponding comprehensive case file of a volunteer than a non-astrologer control subject or random chance, and moreover, didn’t even agree with each other. A study out in 2003, conducted by former astrologer Dr. Geoffrey Dean and psychologist Dr. Ivan Kelly, tracked the lives of 2,000 subjects who were all born within minutes of one another over several decades. The theory was that if astrological claims about star position and birthdates were true, then the individuals would have shared similar traits; they did not. Studies that support the claims of astrology have been largely dismissed by the wider scientific community for a “self-attribution” bias – subjects had a prior knowledge of their sign’s supposed characteristics and therefore could not be reliable – or because they could not be replicated. Astrologers are, unsurprisingly, not impressed by scientific efforts to prove or disprove astrology, claiming that scientists are going about it all wrong – astrology is not empirical in the way that, say, physics is: “Experiments are set up by people who don’t have any context for this, even if they were attempting to do something constructive,” says Shelley von Strunckel, American astrologer and horoscope writer whose column appears in The Sunday Times, London Evening Standard, Chinese Vogue, Tatler and other major publications. “It’s like, ‘I’m going to cook this great French meal, I’ve got this great cook book in French – but I don’t speak French.’”

Dr Strauss says I shoud rite down what I think and remembir and evrey thing that happins to me from now on. — Flowers for Algernon, Daniel Keyes (Rife with spelling and grammatical errors, the line perfectly captures the essence of Charlie’s tale as the reader goes along.) Spoiler alert: “It isn’t.”) Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having nothing to do: once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it had no pictures or conversations in it, “and what is the use of a book,” thought Alice, “without pictures or conversation?” — Alice in Wonderland, Lewis Carroll (You know trouble is brewing when a young one starts to feel bored or restless. Off to an adventure, shall we?) ‘Tom!’ No answer. — The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, Mark Twain (All you need to know about Tom and his ensuing shenanigans, summarized in 3 words. Pithy perfection!) It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness, it was the epoch of belief, it was the epoch of incredulity, it was the season of Light, it was the season of Darkness, it was the spring of hope, it was the winter of despair, we had everything before us, we had nothing before us, we were all going direct to Heaven, we were all going direct the other way - in short, the period was so far like the present period, that some of its noisiest authorities insisted on its being received, for good or for evil, in the superlative degree of comparison only. — A Tale of Two Cities, Charles Dickens (Dickens is indeed the master of openers)

Name: Deepak Mehta
Question: What do you think of this Indian mystic who has survived for 76 years without food and water?
Answer: He didn’t need any food or water because he was powered by bullshit. Sorry, but this needs to be said. All these claims of mystics living for hundreds of years in the Himalayas, or not having eaten in decades is all a charade designed to dupe the unassuming ones. It doesn’t mean that what the late Prahlad Jani had achieved was a small feat. He indeed had so much control over his body that he needed the bare minimum to survive. But the entire claim of not having eaten or drunk anything for seventy years is totally bogus — The man who says he hasn't eaten or drunk for 70 years: Why are eminent doctors taking him seriously? Mr Jani has only been under strict observation twice. Both times under the supervision of the same doctor. Both times for only 15 days. Even during those 15 days, he was allowed to bathe (yes, with water) and sunbathe (which he claims provides him with sustenance). The people who observed him never published their findings in any scientific journal. Nor did they allow any third party to investigate the setting in which he was kept. All we have to go on are their words. They promised to make the findings from the study public, but that never came to pass — DIPAS concludes observational study on ‘Mataji' However, during the second stint of him being monitored, he lost about 4 kgs of weight — https://www.iosrjournals.org/iosr-jrme/papers/Vol-7%20Issue-5/Version-1/J0705015587.pdf For example, the yogi lost some weight during the study and this would be evidence that his claims are wrong, said the head of the Austrian Skeptics Society Dr. Ulrich Berger. Mathematican and head skeptic Berger did more research than James Randi on the case and actually read through the published study and the presentation of Dr. Shah and found that "the daily weight varied between 42 und 38 kilos". So Dr. Berger published as counterevidence that Jani lost 4 kilos from day one to the end of the study. He was also not under 24*7 CCTV surveillance as he was allowed to meet devotees and sunbathe without much supervision. Sanal Edamaruku characterized the experiment as a farce for allowing Jani to move out of the CCTV cameras' field of view, claiming that video footage showed Jani was allowed to receive devotees and to leave the sealed test room for sunbathing. Edamaruku also said that the gargling and bathing activities were insufficiently monitored. Edamaruku was denied access to the site where the tests were conducted in both 2003 and 2010, and accuses Jani of having "influential protectors" responsible for denying him permission to inspect the project during its operation, despite having been invited to join the test during a live television broadcast. Considering all of that, it is a great feat of human endurance, but no miracle. After all, Gandhiji fasted for days on end multiple times during the Independence movement, the longest lasting 21 days.
